name: Lehab
overview: Lehab is a male figure mentioned in the Bible as a son of Mizraim. Beyond this genealogical detail, Scripture provides no additional information about his tribe, lineage, or personal attributes. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical in nature.
namesAndTitles: The name Lehab appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Genesis 10:13. There is no provided meaning or divine origin for the name, and it is presented simply as a proper name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Lehab is identified as the son of Mizraim according to Genesis 10:13. No other family relationships are recorded in Scripture for Lehab beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Lehab’s significance lies in his place within the genealogical record of Genesis 10, which traces the descendants of Noah’s sons and outlines the nations that arose after the Flood. As a son of Mizraim, who is traditionally associated with Egypt, Lehab represents part of the ancestral lineage that contributes to the understanding of the nations known in biblical times. His mention underscores the biblical emphasis on genealogy and the fulfillment of God's sovereign plan through successive generations.
